prompt: What does a language model fundamentally do with your prompt?
explanation: A model generates one token at a time, each time predicting what best continues everything it has seen so far. That's why changing what it sees changes what it writes.

options.text: Looks up the answer in a database of verified facts
Predicts the next token again and again, continuing the text in the way that best fits what it sees
Runs a search engine query and copies the top result
Translates the prompt into code and executes it

prompt: Which of these can be part of a prompt? Select all that apply.
explanation: A prompt holds instructions, context, input data, examples, and format guidance. The model's weights are fixed by training and aren't part of a prompt.

options.text: Instructions describing the task
Background context the model can't know
Examples of the output you want
The model's internal weights

prompt: Small chunks of text, such as whole words, parts of words, or punctuation, that a model reads and writes are called ____.
explanation: Text is split into tokens before the model reads it, and the model generates its answer one token at a time.

items.text: Test the prompt on real inputs
Design a prompt with task, context, and format
Save the version that works and note why
Refine one thing at a time
Inspect the output against what you wanted

prompt: Match each lever to the situation it fits best.

pairs.right: Always the first thing to try
Large or frequently changing information
Live data or exact calculation
A narrow behavior needed at very large scale

prompt: You want answers short enough for a help widget. Which length instruction works best?
explanation: Tokens don't map neatly to words and vary by model, and a token limit truncates rather than shortens. Sentences and word counts are units both you and the model can work with.

options.text: Answer in 50 tokens.
Answer in 2 short sentences, under 40 words.

prompt: Which statements about the context window are true? Select all that apply.
explanation: The context window is everything the model sees in one request, measured in tokens. There's no memory outside it, and research found information in the middle of long contexts is used less reliably.

options.text: It includes the system prompt, the conversation, documents, and the model's own response
It is measured in tokens

Information buried in the middle of a long context is more likely to be missed

prompt: Fluent, confident output that is false or unsupported, such as a made-up citation, is called a ____.
explanation: Models generate plausible text rather than retrieving verified facts, so they can hallucinate specifics like statistics, quotes, and references.

prompt: Why can the same prompt give a different answer each time?
explanation: At each step the model has probabilities for many possible next tokens; sampling from them, rather than always taking the top one, produces variety.

options.text: The model retrains itself after every request
The model picks each token by sampling from a probability distribution
Your internet connection changes the prompt
The model deliberately avoids repeating itself across users

prompt: Order what happens when you send a prompt.

items.text: Tokens are turned back into readable text
Your text is split into tokens
The model computes probabilities for the next token
